predecessors.name: Republic of Vietnam (South Vietnam)
predecessors.text: Tây Ninh Province, where the NLF was founded at Tân Lập village on 20 December 1960, and Bến Tre, where the uprisings that began in January 1960 created 'liberated zones'

successors.name: Socialist Republic of Vietnam
successors.text: all of South Vietnam: the infobox area is 173,809 km2 in 1975; Cliopatria's 1966 outline of the Republic is 180,020 km2

capitals.name: Tây Ninh (NLF headquarters, Tân Lập village)

ledger.x: 1960: the National Liberation Front is founded on 20 December at Tân Lập village in Tây Ninh Province.
1960: the countryside is fought for from the start.
1966: the NLF headquarters withdraws to Memot in Cambodia.
1969: the NLF becomes the Provisional Revolutionary Government on 8 June.
1969: the PRG's capital is Tây Ninh.
1969: the Mekong lowlands are lost.

1972: the PAVN takes Lộc Ninh on 7 April, in the Easter Offensive ('before collapsing under the attack on 7 April'); the page says Lộc Ninh or An Lộc 'would be proclaimed as the capital of the Provisional Revolutionary Government', and the PRG page lists Lộc Ninh as capital 1972-73.
1972: the PRG capital moves from Tây Ninh to Lộc Ninh.
1972: Quảng Trị City falls to the PAVN on 2 May; the advance was 'halted on 5 May at the Mỹ Chánh Line'.
1972: the ARVN retakes Quảng Trị, the Citadel 'finally taken on 16 September', and 'the majority of Quang Tri province'; the north-west around Cam Lộ stays PAVN/PRG.
1973: the PRG capital moves to Cam Lộ in Quảng Trị.
1975: Phước Long falls on 6 January, the first provincial capital the PAVN holds.
1975: Buôn Ma Thuột falls on 18 March and Darlac Province with it.
1975: the Central Highlands are abandoned in mid-March: 'Pleiku and Kon Tum were to be abandoned'.
1975: Huế falls by the end of March.
1975: Đà Nẵng falls on 29 March.
1975: South Vietnam surrenders on 30 April.
1975: the PRG enters Saigon: 'the PRG moved into government offices there' after 30 April.
1975: the war ends with the surrender of 30 April; the original contest zone passes wholly to the PRG.
1976: the PRG merges with the north on 2 July.
1976: the PRG ends and its land is the Socialist Republic of Vietnam's.

wars.name: Vietnam War
wars.outcome: PRG and North Vietnamese victory: Saigon surrendered on 30 April 1975 and the two Vietnams merged on 2 July 1976.

wars.name: Tet Offensive
wars.outcome: 'In January and February 1968, some 80,000 VC struck more than 100 towns'; the offensive did not trigger the general uprising the VC hoped for and moved no border.

wars.name: Easter Offensive
wars.outcome: The PAVN held Lộc Ninh and the north-west of Quảng Trị and the western fringes of II and III Corps, about 10 percent of the country; the ARVN retook Quảng Trị City on 16 September.

wars.name: Ho Chi Minh campaign
wars.outcome: 13 December 1974 to 30 April 1975: Phước Long, Buôn Ma Thuột, Huế, Đà Nẵng, Xuân Lộc and Saigon fall; the Republic of Vietnam surrenders.

certainty.note: A guerrilla zone with no recorded boundary; the pages name only Tây Ninh, Bến Tre, Lộc Ninh and the Cam Lộ area.
From 30 April 1975 the PRG holds the Republic of Vietnam's outline.
